entities.summary: Priscus of Panium was an Eastern Roman diplomat and Greek historian and rhetorician. Born into a prominent family in the Eastern Roman province of Syria, Priscus rose to prominence during the reign of Emperor Theodosius I (r. 378–392 CE), serving as a diplomat and envoy to various regions including the East, Persia, and the Huns. He traveled extensively throughout the world, gathering information on the geography, customs, and cultures of different peoples. Priscus' most significant contribution was his work 'The History', which chronicled his journeys and provided valuable insights into the politics, society, and economy of the Eastern Roman Empire during its decline. This historical text has been lost to time, but fragments remain in various ancient sources, offering a unique window into the world of late antiquity.
